storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Snuggle in, everyone. Today we're reading A Pocket Full of Plops.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Plops! That sounds like a bubbly little word.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I wonder how a plop could fit in a pocket.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Let's open the book and find out together.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Rain tapped the porch roof. Mina pulled on her yellow coat and listened.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Plip, plop, patter-pat! I’ll save some sounds for my family.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A drop landed on a leaf: plip! Mina cupped her hands and tucked the plip into her pocket.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: But the next plip sounded out in the garden. “Stay, little plip, stay!”

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Why does Mina still hear the plip outside? Did it slip out of her pocket?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Her little cupped hands look like a bowl beside that big leaf!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: They do look like a little bowl. But a sound isn't something her hands can hold. Another raindrop makes another plip outside.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A drop landed in a puddle: plop! Mina held her other pocket open wide.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: But the next plop sounded down by her boots. “Stay, little plop, stay!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mina pressed both pockets shut. “Now I’ve got you!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: She peeked inside, but found only a little damp fluff. Plip and plop were still outside.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> That tiny fluff in her pocket looks so soggy!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: So closing both pockets didn't catch the sounds?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: That's right. She found only damp fluff. The plips and plops are still outside, where the rain is falling.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mina went inside and opened her empty hands. “I wanted to bring you the rain.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mama put down her cup. “Then let’s go and listen.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mama came to the porch, and Papa and baby Jo came too. Mina made room beside her.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A leaf went plip; a puddle went plop. Everyone leaned close to listen.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Can you make a plip?” Mina asked. Mama tapped one finger on her cup: tip, tip, tip.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mina grinned. “A tiny sound, just like the leaf!”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Mama's blue cup looks like a tiny drum! Can a little finger make a rain sound?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes! Mama's gentle tap makes a tiny sound like the drop on the leaf. You can try tapping one finger softly on your palm.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Can you make a plop?” Mina asked. Papa patted his knees: pom, pom, pom.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jo clapped, so Mina clapped too. Now their little song had a patter-pat!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Plip, plop, patter-pat!” sang Mina. Mama tapped, Papa patted, and Jo clapped along.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The rain kept time on the roof. They sang it again: “Plip, plop, patter-pat!”

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Did Mina find a way to share the rain sounds without putting them in her pockets?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: She did. They're listening together and making their own sounds with taps, pats, and claps. Even the rain on the roof joins their song.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: At last, the rain grew quiet. Mina’s pockets were empty, but everyone was humming.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: She snuggled close and hummed along. “Plip, plop, patter-pat.”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: I liked sleepy baby Jo. <yawn> Now I feel snuggly too.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Mina's pockets were empty, but everyone had a song to hum.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: You can listen for little sounds with someone you love, too. A quiet moment can hold a lovely song.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Subscribe and come back for our next story. We'll save a cozy spot for you!
